t: A kingdom of the eastern Caucasus between the Kura river and the Caspian, roughly the north and centre of modern Azerbaijan.
A client first of Rome and then of Sasanian Persia, it guarded the Caspian passes against raiders from the steppe.
It adopted Christianity in the 4th century and had its own church and alphabet, whose texts survive in Sinai palimpsests.
dyk: A Roman legion left a Latin inscription at Gobustan near Baku under the emperor Domitian, the easternmost Latin inscription known.
ev: King Oroeses attacks Pompey and is defeated near the Abas river
A detachment of Legio XII Fulminata carves an inscription at Gobustan
King Urnayr adopts Christianity, according to tradition
Albania receives the Armenian provinces of Artsakh and Utik
An alphabet is created for the Caucasian Albanian language
Albanians join the Armenian rising crushed at the Battle of Avarayr
Vachagan III issues church canons at the council of Aghuen
The Sasanians abolish the kingship and rule through marzbans

f.successor: Sasanian Empire; later the Mihranid Principality of Albania
